newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF mission to hold talks in Russia next week.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to hold talks in Russia next week.

text.p: A mission of the International Monetary Fund will arrive in Moscow next week to discuss Russia's economic programme for 1997, a spokeswoman for First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Friday.
Potanin, who is in charge of economic policy, will meet the mission on Tuesday, Larisa Zelkova told Reuters.
The fund and Russian authorities are putting the finishing touches to an economic programme for 1997 as part of the fund's $10 billion loan agreement with Russia.
With the 1997 budget signed into force last week, the way is now clear to put the remaining touches to the plan.

The IMF is pushing for a number of structural changes to the Russian economy, including the reorganisation of natural monopolies, such as gas and electric power, to make their costs more transparent and their charges more equitable.
Russian officials have made it clear they intend to restructure the monopolies, which were attacked on Thursday by President Boris Yeltsin for their high costs and inefficiency.
On Thursday Prime-Tass news agency quoted Potanin as saying that Russia would need several months to decide how to bring competition into monopoly sectors.
But the IMF said Russia was not seeking a delay in negotiations on the programme.
Apart from working on the 1997 programme, which is near completion, the fund is also looking at details of Russian government budget revenues in January and February.
Concern at the low level of revenues has led the fund to delay a decision on disbursement of the January and February tranches of the loan, after payments were repeatedly held up last year.
Revenues fell in January but Russian officials say they picked up again in February.
